steps.body: A square fact multiplies a number by itself: 6 × 6, 7 × 7, 8 × 8.
steps.narration: A square fact multiplies a number by itself: 6 × 6, 7 × 7, 8 × 8.

widget.prompt: Build an array with 6 rows of 6.
widget.factorFeedback: That rectangle covers 36 squares, but not as 6 rows of 6. Build the arrangement the fact describes.
widget.successFeedback: 6 rows of 6 is 36 — a square array.
widget.lowFeedback: That is fewer than 36 squares. Keep building until the array is complete.
widget.highFeedback: That is more than 36 squares. The array should stop at 6 rows of 6.

predict.prompt: What is special about the array for 6 × 6?
predict.reveal: Multiplying a number by itself gives an array as tall as it is wide — a square.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents square facts.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for square facts must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines square facts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 6 × 6 = 36 — one of the table facts worth knowing on sight.

commonErrors.feedback: That is 6 short of the product — one whole group of 6 is missing.
That adds the two factors instead of multiplying them. 6 × 6 means 6 groups of 6.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Skip-count by 6, 6 times — or lean on a fact you already know and adjust.
